commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[finelog] Stop housekeeping and query reads from starving L0 compaction (#11327)

Object compaction on a backlogged table no longer waits behind
housekeeping or query reads:

- A maintenance cycle that ends with compaction work remaining skips
index backfill and runs object collection at most once an hour.
- Compaction reads its inputs through its own cache-read queue.

After #11325, one visit compacted up to 2,048 L0s in about 20 s and then
ran object collection and index backfill while it still held the shared
slot. On the marin hub those two steps took 47 to 1,300 s per visit, and
the net drain fell to about 8,000 L0s per hour with about 176,000
outstanding.

Skipping those steps raised the drain for about 8 minutes after a
restart. Then a 512-input merge that takes 1 s went up to 256 s and the
drain nearly stopped. Queries and compaction shared one 8-permit
cache-read limiter. `FetchLogs` requests over about 24,000 L0s of `log`
each opened roughly 1,000 files and kept that limiter's queue full. The
merge threads used under 0.03 s of CPU in a 5 s sample while they
waited. A merge makes several limiter trips per input, one input at a
time.

With the separate queue deployed on the hub, 512-input merges averaged
1.4 to 3.7 s for the first 14 minutes and compaction removed 58,617 L0s.
The backlog fell from about 126,300 to under 60 L0s per table in 49
minutes, and `FetchLogs` requests succeeded again.

A table that has not collected since process start begins its one-hour
interval at its first backlogged visit, so a restart during a backlog
does not send every table through a full collection.

Index backfill has no time limit under a backlog: a table builds no
index artifacts for new segments until its compaction catches up. A
single query can still fill the query read queue for other queries.

No test covers either change. A cycle ends backlogged only after 20 s of
compaction, which is too large for a unit test.

Part of #11265

[harbor] Stop Mini-SWE at engine rollout budgets (#11407)

Stop Mini-SWE at SkyRL's engine turn and token limits. SkyRL returns
HTTP 400 with `error.type="generation_stopped"` when an engine budget
ends a trial. The stop persists for the rest of the trial, so retries
cannot succeed. Map this terminal response to Mini-SWE's existing
`LimitsExceeded` exit so Harbor can continue verification and retain
earlier tool actions and sampled-token records.

Preserve `ContextLimit` for both context-rejection formats from #11328

rethrows original model failures after the trial, including failures
signaled through the same `generation_stopped` response.

`BadRequestError` after a successful tool turn; it now exits normally
and saves that turn's action, tokens, logprobs and usage. Separate CPU
engine/worker checks exercise actual turn and cumulative token budgets
and confirm that genuine model failures keep the existing failure and
reward policy. These checks use a fixed Harbor grade; no live verifier
was run.

Add a single-device Gated DeltaNet-2 TPU kernel (#9350)

Add an experimental single-device Gated DeltaNet-2 Pallas kernel for
Levanter. Compute off-diagonal scores with boundary-centered matrix
products and mask noncausal diagonal pairs before exponentiation. The

recurrent state.

seven input gradients. The benchmark, tuning cache, TPU stage probes,
and historical measurement snapshots live in the GDN-2 research archive.

the refactored kernel.

commits.author: davidlundgren
commits.message:
[eval] Seed GPU evaluation runs by default (#11312)

Adds a default seed (when applicable) for eval runs.

Part of #9558

<details>
<summary>:robot: Full description</summary>

The evaluation launcher now gives curated runs seed 0 when neither
`--seed` nor the selection's `run.seed` is set. Benchmarks are
unchanged: none declares a seed or a temperature.

#10957 kept the legacy launcher's behavior of sending no seed. A served
model that samples then returns different replies on every run. In
#9558, two runs of the same frozen Snowball checkpoint matched on 3 of
164 HumanEval+ replies and scored 51.83% and 42.07%.

The seed is a property of the launch. A shared default makes standard
runs repeat, so a surprising score can be regenerated and inspected. It
does not make a score more accurate: a seeded score is still one draw,
and decisions that rest on small differences still need several seeds or
paired intervals.

The default applies only where the endpoint accepts per-request seeds.
Marin's TPU vLLM rejects a request that combines a seed with a
temperature above zero (`tpu_inference/platforms/tpu_platform.py`: "JAX
does not support per-request seed"), so TPU vLLM runs stay unseeded
unless a seed is given. An explicit seed is sent on every platform.

On GPU the run seed changes from none to 0. The seed is part of each
run's identity, so existing GPU runs are executed again at their next
launch instead of being reused. TPU run identities and all prepared
corpora are unchanged.

Three launches of Qwen3-0.6B on HumanEval+ (one H100 each,
batch-invariant vLLM, cw-rno2a, sampling at the model's temperature 0.6)
check that the seed reaches the server. Each run records the request it
sent per sample.

| Launch | Seed given | Seed in all requests | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | none | 0 | 25.61% |
| B | none | 0 | 164 of 164 replies and grades identical to A |
| C | `--seed 7` | 7 | 24 of 164 replies identical to A; 29.88% |

A and B ran on separate servers and agree exactly while sampling, which
requires the server to honor the seed. C shows the seed value changes
the samples.

Identical replies across runs also need deterministic serving:
single-GPU batch-invariant vLLM as here, or the #10760 profile for
multi-GPU Snowball.

Earlier commits on this branch declared seeds and temperatures in each
benchmark and set Snowball's temperature; later commits revert the first
and move the second to #11398, so the net diff is the launcher default,
its test and the docs. #11065 made a related fix in the launcher that
#10957 deleted and is superseded by this change. A checked-in
repeatability command remains open.

</details>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[finelog] Drain object-backed L0 backlogs within one maintenance visit (#11325)

Object-backed tables now drain an L0 backlog several jobs at a time. An
L0 compaction job takes up to 512 inputs instead of 32, and one
maintenance visit repeats compaction while work remains, for up to 20
seconds. L1 and L2 jobs keep the 32-input cap, and promotion still
starts at 32 segments.

On the marin hub, all 35 object-backed tables share two `QueryServing`
maintenance slots. Each visit ran one 32-input job, and the follow-up
visit that pending work requests queued behind every other table. From
2026-11-12, busy tables added 600–700 L0s per ~12-minute round while
compacting 32. `log` reached 21,237 L0s averaging 135 KB. Each L0 spans
the whole key range, so every `FetchLogs` and time-bounded query opened
them all and failed with `snapshot read deadline exceeded`. Hub logs
over 46 minutes showed 32-input jobs taking a median 9.5 s to merge and
2.2 s to upload, all from cache, with slot waits of 12 minutes at the
median.

A cycle that runs at least 5 seconds now logs `slow maintenance cycle
step breakdown` with per-step wall time. The hub logs showed turns of
324–893 s that the merge lines do not explain. The 512 cap bounds how
long one job holds a shared slot, since an in-flight job runs to
completion.

Part of #11265

commits.message:
[levanter] Preserve packed Snowball attention across context shards (#11370)

Shard Splash kernel mask metadata with the query and head axes so
Snowball can execute packed attention on four context shards.
Replicating global query positions previously caused a lowering failure
when 512 positions reached a 128-query shard.

Add Snowball packed-document hidden-state and loss isolation checks on a
single device and four context shards. The segment-ID adapter correction
already landed in #10492; the missing coverage includes blockwise flash
attention and hardware-gated FA4/CuTe and Splash paths.

Require exact isolation when another packed document changes. A
single-segment mask must match unsegmented causal attention bit for bit,
separately on one device and four context shards. Compile the test
forward with deterministic XLA operations: ordinary BF16 executions can
differ by 0.0078125 even on identical inputs, which can obscure an
attention-boundary regression. Keep the existing FP32 checks comparing
context-parallel and unsharded values and gradients.

The broad affected suite finished with 1,144 passes, 331 skips and five
checkpoint-path failures; all five reproduce independently on unchanged
main at `6eb54e9d34`. The real FA4/CuTe case passed on four H100s at
sequence length 1024. Splash value and gradient checks pass in CPU
interpretation; native execution is hardware-gated for TPU CI.

Correct stale packing guidance while retaining the recipes' `pack=False`
defaults. Enabling packing for a separate experiment requires
`SFTSpec.pack=True` and a new `SFTSpec.version`; the launcher selects a
separate packed preprocessing cache.

Fixes #9029.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Batch and throttle checkpoint uploads to respect Hub commit limits (#10898)

Commit up to eight checkpoint shards at once and pace every Hub commit,
including request and completion metadata. A 193-shard checkpoint needs
25 weight commits instead of 193. With at most four concurrent uploaders
and no other commit-producing writers, the 75-second interval before the
first commit and after each commit response keeps the workers below the
observed 256-commits/hour repository limit.

Repository commit-limit responses back off for at least one hour even if
generic API headers specify a shorter delay. Each commit gets at most
four retries after its initial HTTP 429 response; other failures
propagate. Eight largest Hero shards use about 58 GB of staging disk per
worker.

Require the repository to match the configured expected visibility
before preparing an upload and before every commit. Private remains the
default; uploading to an existing public repository requires explicit
`expected_visibility: public`. The uploader never changes repository
visibility. Expected visibility is a delivery setting outside the
immutable export and upload request identities, so verified checkpoints
can resume after an intentional visibility change.

Version-2 CPU export manifests validate the complete original export
configuration; version-3 manifests retain artifact-only comparison.
Existing Hub shards must match source size and SHA-256. The completion
marker follows weight verification at a pinned commit and exact
model-card and license verification.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[shellbox] Centralize Daytona snapshot identity and reclamation (#11202)

Move Daytona snapshot source selection, resource rounding, naming and
preparation out of Harbor's environment adapter and into Shellbox.
Harbor's adapter maps its task configuration onto a `MachineSpec`
through one validated helper, and Shellbox derives the snapshot identity
and machine request from it. Account credentials live in a single
`DaytonaConnection` with the API key hidden from `repr`; field
validation happens when a client factory is built, so hosts that do not
use Daytona stay constructible and Harbor creates its provider client
lazily.

Add `shellbox-daytona-snapshots` to inventory an account, compare it
with a required set, create missing snapshots and purge stale ones after
revalidating last use. One classification serves the inventory, the dry
run and the revalidation, and a snapshot whose last-use evidence
disappears between the inventory and the revalidation is recorded as
unclassified instead of aborting the purge. The driver's
`snapshot-specs` command emits the resulting `SnapshotRequest`
interchange, after applying the job's resource overrides and enforcement
policy and an optional runtime overlay, so preflight resolves the task
set the run actually launches without provider credentials.
`.agents/ops/daytona.md` records the one-hour account-wide purge policy
and the exact commands.

Snapshot names are unchanged: `shellbox-` plus the first 40 hex
characters of `sha256(image_source_key(source) + json(resources))`, so
existing snapshots remain reusable. Registry images are identified by
reference, so moving a tag keeps its snapshot name; Docker build
contexts are identified by their current contents. The task GPU count
now participates in the identity.

[shellbox] Run local sandboxes on NixOS (#11311)

Run local Shellbox sandboxes on NixOS with two read-only mounts: `/nix/store` and the system program profile at `/run/current-system/sw`. Host-program commands and transfers search the profile's `bin` directory; OCI image machines use their own environment. Managed Python requires `nix-ld` on the host.

The store mount exposes host configuration stored there by its store path. On the NixOS test host, the two-mount variant measured 45 ms median machine creation versus 620 ms for 567 dependency mounts, with warm caches and a quota of one CPU. See the [startup comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11311#discussion_r4560581567).

Replace the sandbox's read-only `/etc/hosts` copy before writing task hostnames. Factory failures retain bubblewrap's underlying startup error.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Alert on idle GB200 cluster capacity (#11115)

Alert when fewer than 10% of Ready GB200 GPUs have more than 10%
utilization for 30 minutes. The bridge compares the last five minutes of
node-agent telemetry with Kubernetes GPU capacity per cluster and sends
the warning to the operator Slack route. A GPU counts as active when any
sample in the window exceeds the utilization threshold. The notification
includes the active GPU percentage, the Ready GPU count, and an
accelerator dashboard link.

The bridge decides idleness and reports it as a 0 or 1 alert value, so
the thresholds live only in `b200_utilization_alert.py`. Each cluster
row also carries a `state` label: `idle`, `active`,
`telemetry_incomplete` (telemetry covers less than 80% of Ready
capacity), `capacity_unavailable` (the Kubernetes node listing failed),
or `no_ready_capacity`. Only `idle` fires. Grafana shows the label, so a
cluster that cannot be measured is distinguishable from an active one.
Ready capacity is a numeric annotation query, so node churn does not
reset the pending timer; a change of `state` does.

A count over the same five-minute window of `telemetry_v1.node_agent`
took about 11 seconds on the hub from a developer machine on 2026-11-12,
against a 20-second bridge query timeout. A query that times out reports
`telemetry_incomplete` and does not fire. The `$values` annotations in
the summary have not been rendered on a live Grafana.

Fixes #11114

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Typed recipes (4/4): Validate every recipe path with typed classes (#10643)

Validate a SkyRL recipe with the typed recipe classes in
`lib/skyrlrecipe` on every path that builds one: the vendored launcher,
the local OPD runners, and the edits experiments make to a recipe. A
wrong key, value type, or option value fails with an error that names
the field, before a GPU job starts.

The launcher validates the recipe in a training launch document with
`SkyRLRecipe.from_document` before Hydra merges SkyRL's base config, so
YAML recipes such as `vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/configs/*.yaml` get the
same checks and error messages as recipes built by experiments. A
training document with an empty `runtime.entrypoint`, which is what
Marin submits, always takes this path; a document the launcher has
already composed is reloaded as written. The launcher reads the context
budget, engine options, and entrypoint from the validated recipe. The
SkyRL entrypoint modules expose `run(cfg)` and have no command line of
their own; the launcher, the OPD runners, and the tests call it. The
launcher checks the node count against the role plan and the runtime
profile against `trainer.strategy`, and it rejects a `trainer.placement`
GPU count larger than the allocation's GPUs per node. A launch document
must set `inputs.data_kind`; the launcher rejects one whose value
differs from the recipe's `data.kind`, and a recipe that sets
`data.train_data` or `data.val_data` when the launch document supplies
data inputs. When a recipe does not set
`generator.num_inference_engines`, the engine count is the allocation's
GPUs divided by the inference tensor-parallel size, which defaults to 4.
An object-store draft model must name a `sha256:` identity, which the
task runtime compares with the model's manifest before staging it.

The schema covers the callback options at main `2af3f828aa`: the
checkpoint callbacks accept `save_after_fraction`, and `best_checkpoint`
accepts `selection_metric` and `preservation_max_drop`. A test checks
that each declared callback's fields equal its constructor's parameters.
`generator.backend` and the trajectory-retention `inference_backend`
accept only `vllm`. A recipe that sets `checkpoint_export` is rejected
with a message that the launch document owns export settings.
`Section.replace` returns a validated copy of a section with the given
fields changed.

The H100 OPD nightly (`ci/marin_nightly/opd.py`, run by
`run_opd_h100.sh`) and `examples/cat_count/gpu_opd.py` build a
`SkyRLRecipe` with the declared teacher and routing types, and
`examples/recipe.py` composes it with SkyRL's base config.

Experiments keep a `SkyRLRecipe` through every edit, change it with
`merge(RecipePatch(...))`, `with_settings`, or `Section.replace`, and
convert it to YAML where it is passed to `SkyRLSpec`.
`experiments/post_training/snowball_online_eagle.py` builds its
draft-model training settings, Megatron geometry, and role plan directly
from the typed classes. The launch-document census fails when an
experiment module that constructs a `SkyRLSpec` is missing from it.

After loading, the launch and task documents from every experiment are
identical to those at main `2af3f828aa`. The bundled recipes in
`vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/configs` compose, load, and persist to the same
configs as at main; `snowball_mopd_ultra_32k.yaml` leaves
`trainer.max_ckpts_to_keep` to the launch document. The local OPD
configs equal main's with three differences:
`generator.use_conversation_multi_turn` and
`generator.require_exact_chat_transport`, which the schema rejects and
no runtime code reads, are absent; distillation and teacher fields are
in schema order; and the nightly sets `trainer.resume_mode` to `none`
where main's config has null, both of which start without resuming. On
H100s, the OPD nightly lane passes on this branch and the cat-count
lane's training job succeeds (Iris job
`/runner/skyrl-nightly-cat-count-h100-43353780133-1-a1`).

Part of marin-community/MarinSkyRL#933.

---------

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Complete migration to curated TaskSpec evaluations (#10957)

Run the evaluation CLI, training checkpoint menus and the [September 25, 2026 publication campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/weaver/evalchemy-finish-migration/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled) against canonical TaskSpec corpora. Remove `vendor/evalchemy` and its execution, packaging and CI paths, completing the launcher and consumer handoff from #10757. Evaldash derives summaries from recorded protocol metadata and keeps historical Evalchemy scores available for comparisons without model reruns.

Evaluation configuration owns supported protocols, shot counts and request formats. Dataset records contain pinned source populations and support files. Benchmark modules keep each dataset beside its evaluation bindings; shared curation code supplies acquisition and catalog integration. Callers select these settings through `EvaluationSelection`. Preparation binds them to the reusable TaskCompendium compilers before publication; runtime consumes the resulting immutable operations. GSM8K zero-shot and five-shot evaluations share the dataset declaration and acquisition artifact; evaluation preparation compiles separate immutable prompt corpora for each protocol. MMLU owns its subject partitions. Its launch configuration no longer enumerates 57 source IDs. Benchmark families declare chat-template policy, grading, metrics, sampling, trial seeds and context rules. Shared builders receive those settings explicitly. Evalchemy protocols inherit the serving model’s temperature and request seed unless the caller overrides them, preserving the legacy launcher’s sampling behavior.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Benchmark data: pinned population and support examples] --> B[Evaluation configuration: protocol, shots, format and partitions]
    B --> C[Acquire source rows and demonstration pools]
    B --> D[Build locked grader environment]
    C --> E[Evaluation preparation: compile final TaskSpec prompts and operations]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Validate complete population and protocol]
    F --> G[Publish immutable corpus and manifest]
    G --> H[Publish canonical catalog snapshot separately]
```

Ordinary benchmark defaults need no launcher YAML. One `configs/evalchemy.yaml` contains suite choices and run overrides; the publication campaign has its own selection document. Per-evaluation mapping files, source-name aliases, shot-group searches and dynamic checkpoint alias registration are removed. The shared choice compiler assembles requests from explicit layouts and sampling rules, including reversed Winogrande demonstrations. Named presets carry actual protocol choices or run policy, such as a smoke limit or judge deployment. Checkpoint pipelines pass typed selections directly to the shared launcher. Model-dependent prompt format is resolved once and recorded explicitly. Unsupported combinations fail before inference. Runtime limits never truncate the published population.

The launcher pins model and tokenizer revisions and materializes the selected corpus dependencies in the serving cluster's storage region before starting shared candidate inference. Corpus references include the publication recipe and version independently of storage placement. Executors receive resolved artifact roots. Catalog snapshot publication remains a separate curation operation. The driver reads the running server's context limit, admits source rows under the recorded cohort and context policies, expands the declared trials and executes likelihood, completion or chat operations. Python and instruction graders run through Shellbox. The orchestrator uses the privileged Iris container profile so grader children can inherit it; checkpoint pipeline parents need the same profile. Workers use the task image's Python 3.12 for namespace and pidfd interfaces.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[CLI, checkpoint or campaign: typed selections and model] --> B[Freeze supported protocol and prompt format]
    B --> C[Materialize pinned corpus dependencies]
    C --> D[Start shared candidate inference]
    D --> E[Admit source rows and expand trials]
    E --> F[Execute operations and packaged graders or configured judges]
    F --> G[FineStore: configuration, selection ledger, attempts and samples]
    G --> H[Evaldash: select terminal retries and reduce declared metrics]
    H --> I[Protocol comparisons, coverage and sample browser]
    G --> J[Resume completed work and retry infrastructure failures]
    J --> E
```

Workers persist raw observations and run references. Request concurrency affects scheduling without changing scoring or resume identity. Evaldash owns means, weighted means, classification rates, perplexity reductions and grouped summaries. Perplexity follows declared log-likelihood metadata. PIQA uses character-normalized likelihood accuracy as its headline. Local ingestion and PostgreSQL reconciliation share the importer; reconciliation tracks archive revisions so resumed results refresh without rewriting producer records. Summaries and sample browsing select the same latest finished attempt per logical trial, including failed grades. Valid zero scores remain scored, retries do not enlarge denominators, and coverage separates full population, selected trials and scored trials.

Panels and comparisons expose benchmark protocol variants separately. A newer five-shot run cannot displace the same model's zero-shot result. Corpus comparison identities bind source, compiler, grader and protocol independently of regional paths and conversion timing; physical manifest hashes protect integrity and resume. Known differing corpus identities remain incompatible. Protocol metadata and recorded selections must agree.

Historical Evalchemy labels are interpreted at the reader boundary using their known protocol choices, recorded shot counts and prompt format. Shared metric normalization maps likelihood `acc,none`, code-task `pass@1`/`pass_at_1` and MRCR `mrcr_accuracy` to `accuracy`; `normalized_accuracy` and F1 stay distinct. Raw metric maps retain their original spellings and extraction filters. Compatible historical scores can join native protocol columns without rewriting archives or rerunning inference. Recorded shot counts and prompt formats must agree when present; missing historical values do not alone exclude a score. Existing native archives without semantic corpus identities use the same checks. Comparisons retain each score's cohort and the warning about differing evaluation settings. New curated runs must use new cohort labels: the verified Evalchemy cohorts pin the historical evaluator implementation, so reusing those labels would misstate how a score was produced.

External judges require deployment identities and secret references. Provider-managed aliases identify the deployment/model without promising immutable provider weights. The publication campaign records its separately served policy judge and finishes an evaluation as `artifact_failed` when any benchmark scores fewer than 90% of selected logical trials. Harbor retains its separate runtime. Evaldash requires an application release to serve the new summaries and protocol comparisons in production.

[skyrl] Centralize backend validation and simplify remote inference (#11292)

@penfever Sorry for the for the automerge of #11230, addressing your 2
nits here!
___
Move the existing check for `generator.backend='vllm'` from Megatron
validation to the start of shared generator validation. Unsupported
values now raise a `ValueError` that names `generator.backend`.
Evaluation already rejected unsupported backends before starting Ray;
the check's ownership and error are now explicit.

Remove the remote HTTP client's unused backend selector and redundant
branches. OpenAI-compatible request forwarding, sampled token IDs and
logprobs, and vLLM management requests keep their existing behavior.
Follow-up to the two review nits in #11230.

The frozen SkyRL CPU lane passed 448 tests, including six HTTP
regressions; the affected launcher test also passed. Startup probes
confirm that training and evaluation reject unsupported backends before
Ray starts and that valid vLLM configuration passes generator
validation.

commits.message:
[rl] Add agent protocol probe tasks and an offline fetch tool (#11049)

We were seeing errors
([marin-community/marin#10393](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10393))
with snowball v0.1 struggling a bit with tool-calling adherence (e.g.,
not making a required file and simulating tool execution without actual
tool calling).

This PR adds a extra debugging and logging infra to monitor these
separately from answer correctness. We track:

* required-file submission
* tool execution
* ~thinking disabled~
* URL loading

I evaled [snowball v0.1
here](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/codex/32-protocol-probes).
